- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model underestimates the continuation of the trend (overshoot followed by premature correction).
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model too quickly brings prices back to historical averages, ignoring recent momentum.
- Forecasts for the last 5–10 days are often too low, suggesting underestimation of late-period volatility or policy-driven spikes.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing sustained upward trends — delays in adjusting forecasts when price momentum is clear.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture abrupt reversals or sudden policy-driven price jumps.
- Overconfidence in short-term momentum leads to overestimation of price increases in the first 10 days, then underestimation of the long-term trend.
